rules.statement: MWM instructions and approved decisions control local integrity scope, release authority, and author-preserving boundaries.
COPE, ICMJE, CSE, Crossref, CRediT/NISO, ORI, COS, and other external frameworks inform process only within explicit MWM delegation.
A substantive integrity result requires identified chapter/version/stage, governing authorities, confidentiality permissions, citation graph status, source-access log, and case ownership.
Quotations, participant details, author correspondence, allegations, reviewer material, confidential manuscripts, raw data, contact information, and legal/ethics materials are protected records.
Use neutral observable signal language and reserve formal misconduct terms for quoted authority findings or authorized human records.
Every material finding preserves exact text/locator, source or record, access status, comparison/basis, authority, owner, next action, confidence, escalation, and closure condition.
No integrity case closes without an authorized owner; institutional, source-owner, publisher, legal/ethics, security, and author-group questions are routed.
Claim-to-source review compares content, scope, population, date, direction, causal language, certainty, modality, and limitations.
Quoted text, omissions, insertions, ellipses, attribution, translation markers, locators, and paraphrase meaning must be compared with the available source.
Author, title, year, edition/version, DOI/URL, and cited object are matched against the intended source identity and reference graph.
Correction, retraction, withdrawal, expression-of-concern, preprint, new version, and supersession statuses remain distinct and date-stamped.
Similarity or overlap is an evidence-backed lead requiring source spans, context, attribution, and human review; it is never itself a plagiarism finding.
Byline, contributor, acknowledgment, affiliation, correspondence, and declarations are compared for coherence; authorship entitlement and order are not decided by CEI.
Funding, conflicts, ethics, consent, data/code/materials, registration/protocol, permissions, and AI-use declarations are checked against the applicable local matrix.

Incompatible names, dates, numbers, sample sizes, populations, methods, tables, figures, and source statuses are flagged only when they refer to the same object and cannot be explained by version, subgroup, or history.
AI-use records include tool/version, date, purpose, material processed, authorization, accepted/edited/rejected output, human reviewer, and required disclosure.
Unapproved external processing of confidential manuscript or sensitive material is a critical confidentiality event requiring immediate evidence preservation and security/senior escalation.
Serious concerns, authorship disputes, source-owner status, institutional, publisher, legal/ethics, and security matters are referred without unauthorized investigation or public allegation.
Choose the least consequential proportionate remedy: pass, query, qualify, correct, replace_source, hold, refer, notice, or block.
Release-affecting source, manuscript, status, response, and decision changes retain version lineage and superseded evidence.
The integrity report includes scope, limitations, open/resolved/blocked summary, evidence, responses, decisions, release effect, unresolved risk, and next trigger.

Release is blocked by unresolved high/critical cases, central source-unavailable quotations, disputed authorship changes, confidentiality incidents, materially stale central sources, missing mandatory disclosures, or unapproved public-status remedies.
A source-status concern, overlap lead, historical name, disclosure, or claim may close with no action after evidence-based review; no finding is forced.
local, live, web_only, author_supplied, inaccessible, stale, and unknown source states are recorded distinctly; source_unavailable cannot become verified without evidence.
Central claims, quotations, contributor records, confidentiality events, and public-status changes receive a higher review and release threshold than incidental issues.
Author, source-owner, or institutional responses are preserved as evidence and do not erase or silently overwrite the original finding.
Meaning-bearing internal contradictions are routed to the relevant statistical, technical, source, or integrity owner; CEI does not choose the plausible value.
Every referred case identifies authorized destination, neutral issue description, evidence to preserve, requested decision, and release effect.
Protected content is processed only through approved tools and access paths; unapproved exposure is never normalized as ordinary review.
Each release-affecting remedy has a decision owner, authority, evidence considered, response summary, proportionate rationale, release effect, approval date, and supersession state.

formal_terms_policy: Formal terms such as plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, misconduct, fraud, and bad faith require an authorized human determination or quotation of an authoritative record; otherwise use neutral signal language.
